newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean chipmakers hit '97 high on profit hopes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean chipmakers hit '97 high on profit hopes.

text.p: Shares of three South Korean chipmakers hit new 1997 highs in early morning trading on Tuesday as investors bet that rebounding prices for memory chips would boost profits in the companies this year, brokers said.
South Korea's largest chipmaker Samsung Electronics rose 1,200 won to 65,000 against its previous 1997 high of 64,300.
LG Electroncis gained 1,600 won to 30,600 and Hyundai Electronics added 1,700 won to 41,600.
Brokers said the unit price for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips rose to $10 to $11 recently from less than $10 in recent months.
"Investors believe the price rise will help the chipmakers post high profits this year," said a Tongyang Securities analyst.
